parts.description: Claude Code skill encoding the full conda-forge recipe lifecycle. 3-tier architecture: canonical scripts + CLI wrappers + data state. The lifecycle is 9 numbered steps plus 3 lettered sub-steps (1b, 7a/7b, 8b) = 12 gated stages; CLAUDE.md refers to it as 'the 10-step loop'. One human-gated checkpoint at step 8b (prepare_submission_branch). Authoritative spine: SKILL.md (3,887 lines) — 6 `## Operating Principles`, 12 `## Critical Constraints` subsections, gotchas G1–G107 (contiguous, no gaps).

parts.description: Offline-tolerant package-intelligence pipeline that builds and maintains cf_atlas.db (SQLite, schema v29) inventorying conda-forge packages (working set) plus a separate pypi_universe side table (the full PyPI directory) plus a pypi_intelligence enrichment side table indexed on pypi_name plus three external-catalog overlay tables: cisa_kev (CISA KEV catalogue; v8.5.3+), epss_scores (FIRST.org EPSS daily CSV; v8.6.0+), cwe_categories (MITRE CWE Research Concepts view with a 67-entry cf_atlas seed mapping → 7 categories + 'Other'; v8.6.0+). 22 executable phases (B→N plus O/P/Q/R/S, with B.5/B.6/C.5/E.5/G' sub-phases) with TTL gates and checkpoint-aware resumption. Air-gap-tolerant via S3-parquet (Phase F) and cf-graph offline (Phase H) backends. v7.9.0 actionable-scope audit closed phase-denominator drift across Phase H/J/M and split Phase D into daily-lean + TTL-gated universe upsert. v8.0.0 structural-enforcement + persona-profiles bundle ships the v_actionable_packages view (7 phase selectors refactored) + Phase H serial-aware eligible-rows gate (warm-daily ~5 min → ~30 s) + tests/meta/test_actionable_scope.py + bootstrap-data --profile {maintainer,admin,consumer}. v8.1.0 PyPI intelligence layer adds 5 phases (O snapshot-based activity_band; P BigQuery downloads opt-in; Q cross-channel BOOLs; R per-project JSON enrichment for a top-N candidate slice; S computed conda_forge_readiness + recommended_template), the pypi-intelligence CLI + MCP tool, and the v_pypi_candidates view. v8.5.3 (Path C) adds the cisa_kev overlay via a direct CISA JSON pull instead of `vdb --cache-os` (which would have downloaded ~33 GB and still left vuln_kev_affecting_current=0 because appthreat-vulnerability-db hardcodes `kevc` in DEFAULT_IGNORE_SOURCE_PATTERNS); v8.5.3 (DW12) ships the v_current_version_vulns query-time-correct view + the _phase_g_sync_current_rollup pure-SQL tail step on Phase G'. v8.6.0 AppThreat Deep Signals adds epss_scores + cwe_categories side tables + 4 packages columns + 3 package_version_vulns columns + fetch-epss / fetch-cwe-catalog CLIs. NOTE (2026-07-25): `src/shared/packages/pyforge-atlas/` is a Kedro/Dagster/DuckDB PARALLEL REIMPLEMENTATION of this pipeline, explicitly NOT a replacement — see Part 5 and the CHANGELOG v8.79.0 entry.

parts.description: BMAD-METHOD v6.10.0 installer + multi-project planning layout, with a separately-managed SKF module v2.0.1 layered on (`_bmad/_config/skf-manifest.yaml`). Six-layer config merge; 93 directories under .claude/skills/ = 89 real skills + 4 non-skill support dirs. Hosts 14 BMAD projects in a single repo. Active-project resolution is `--project <slug>` > `BMAD_ACTIVE_PROJECT` > `_bmad/custom/.active-project` marker > none. CRITICAL: the marker is only HALF the switch — two gitignored symlinks, `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts -> projects/<slug>/planning-artifacts` and `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts -> projects/<slug>/implementation-artifacts`, are the other half, because `_bmad/bmm/config.yaml` hard-codes `planning_artifacts: {project-root}/_bmad-output/planning-artifacts` and that key does NOT compose with a project's `output_folder` override. Marker and symlinks must always agree; `scripts/bmad-switch` re-points the symlinks atomically and writes the marker last. HARD RULE (2026-07-25): parallel agents MUST address projects by physical path and MUST NOT call `scripts/bmad-switch` — it mutates per-working-tree global state that no agent holds a lock on. Execution is driven by `bmad-loop`, an external deterministic orchestrator.

parts.description: Five hatchling-built Python distributions under `src/shared/packages/`, sharing a PEP 420 IMPLICIT namespace: `pyforge`. There is deliberately NO `src/pyforge/__init__.py` in any of them (verified absent in all five), which is what lets `pyforge.atlas`, `pyforge.doctor`, `pyforge.herald`, `pyforge.scribe` and `pyforge.warden` coexist as separately-installable distributions. Each package carries its own `[package]` pixi.toml (a pixi workspace member) and NO `[workspace]` table. Cross-package edges are one-directional and extras-gated (atlas→warden, doctor→warden via the `gate` extra); nothing imports in reverse. Each package's exit-code projection has a single owner module, `verdict.py`. In brand prose these are the PyForge Smiths; `pyforge` lowercase is the technical form only (dists, modules, slugs, paths, envs, branches, CLIs).

integration_points.details: Both parts read/write .claude/data/conda-forge-expert/ — cf_atlas.db is Part 2's primary artifact; Part 1's edit_recipe / scan_for_vulnerabilities / generate_recipe_from_pypi consume it via query helpers.

Each MCP tool in conda_forge_server.py imports from .claude/skills/conda-forge-expert/scripts/<module>.py and forwards args. The MCP server is the wire format; the canonical implementation is Part 1's scripts.
Atlas-intelligence tools (query_atlas, package_health, staleness_report, etc.) read cf_atlas.db directly via the canonical scripts in Part 1.

Every BMAD agent (planning, dev, review, retro) touching conda-forge work MUST invoke the conda-forge-expert skill via the Skill tool. Codified in CLAUDE.md § 'BMAD ↔ conda-forge-expert integration'. The skill's lifecycle (9 numbered steps + 3 lettered sub-steps 1b / 7a-7b / 8b = 12 gated stages; CLAUDE.md calls it 'the 10-step loop') plus its Operating Principles and Critical Constraints override BMAD story instructions when they conflict.

Every BMAD effort that did conda-forge work runs bmad-retrospective at closeout. Retro findings update SKILL.md, reference/*.md, guides/*.md, and CHANGELOG.md. Skill version bumps per semver (PATCH for fixes, MINOR for new gotchas, MAJOR for breaking workflow changes). Codified in CLAUDE.md § 'BMAD ↔ conda-forge-expert integration'.

Two edges. (1) GOVERNANCE: every tracked file under src/shared/packages/ must be covered by a spec `surface:` glob or an explicit allowlist entry, enforced by scripts/spec_surface_check.py — the same contract that governs the rest of the repo. (2) PACKAGING: the `*-build-conda` pixi tasks build these distributions into conda artifacts (dist-conda/ exists for warden and atlas), so any recipe work on them is conda-forge-expert territory and triggers the Rule-1 skill-invocation requirement.

pyforge-atlas re-expresses the cf_atlas pipeline on Kedro + Dagster + Parquet/Ibis-DuckDB across 7 Kedro pipelines. The skill CHANGELOG v8.79.0 entry states explicitly that it does NOT replace the legacy 22-executable-phase SQLite pipeline in Part 2; both exist. Do not describe either as superseding the other.

pyforge-atlas and pyforge-doctor each declare `gate = [pyforge-warden]` as an optional extra — one-directional, opt-in compliance gating. Nothing imports in reverse. doctor's gate extra is declared but not yet wired. Each package projects its own exit codes through a single owner module, verdict.py.

pyforge/atlas/mcp/server.py is an independent FastMCP server exposing 11 tools. It does not extend, wrap, or replace the 46-tool legacy server at .claude/tools/conda_forge_server.py — the repo now runs two distinct MCP surfaces.

Every outbound HTTP request from Parts 1, 2, 3 routes through .claude/skills/conda-forge-expert/scripts/_http.py — truststore (native CA) + JFrog X-JFrog-Art-Api header (when JFROG_API_KEY set) + GitHub token + .netrc fallback. CRITICAL: JFROG_API_KEY leaks to every host when set; mitigation patterns in docs/reference/enterprise-deployment.md § Cross-host credential leak.

vuln-db pixi env provides the AppThreat vulnerability database (NVD + GHSA + OSV + npm + custom sources). Part 1's scan_for_vulnerabilities and Part 2's Phase G/G' read from .claude/data/conda-forge-expert/vdb/. A separate env keeps the default local-recipes env lean.

rebuild_dependencies.reasoning: BMAD infra must exist for any planning to happen — nothing else is authored without a Dream and a Spec. The skill (Part 1) is foundational: Parts 2 and 3 are essentially extensions of it (Part 2 = the data pipeline encoded in the skill's scripts/; Part 3 = the MCP wire format over the skill's scripts/). Part 5 comes last for two independent reasons: pyforge-atlas is a parallel reimplementation of Part 2 and needs Part 2's semantics to exist as its reference, and every package in Part 5 is governed by a spec surface (bmad-infra) and shipped as a conda artifact through Part 1's tooling. Build order matches dependency order.
